Name: Stephanie Bassman
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

Using a version of the Atwoodian table while doing this - to help them keep track the info in the texts, they really got into this. I was worried they would think it silly. I think we all go with the one and done theory and this proves again that repetition and adding layers is helpful. Unfortunately, I found myself hurrying and should not be. Organization is still an issue-helping them keep these ready for the next day...not having to start over because they lost their papers. I am now keeping this project in the classroom to prevent that.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
One student well known for sleeping as often as possible- stayed awake for this. As suspected the girls added a bit to the atwoodian table-----if made them happy I figured it would hold their interest. Some commented that adding the table to the mix helped them feel like they were putting a face on the facts.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
I think this is a cycle worth repeating especially when doing debate or argumentative writing, but also for straight research and checking credibility. It seems to be something they can start on their own after doing it a couple of times, and that it will be automatically helpful for them as they get used to it. Adding different media to this mix will be the next step for me.
